lessonsLearned.text: LDT carries its own style guard for the very thing this wave touches: `pe-r1-brief-flood.test.ts > F2 flood prose is withheld while the citation is degraded > no summary string, emitted or in source, contains an em dash` reads r1BriefCompose.ts AS SOURCE and failed the whole api-server Test job on one em dash in a new JSDoc comment (the emitted sentence was clean). Write new comments em-dash-free; a sibling guard for the panel and the sheet is the obvious next port.

Raising a shared-type package's pin in ONE manifest of a pnpm workspace is worse than not raising it at all. LDT's api-server went to ^1.36.0 while six sibling manifests stayed at ^1.34.0; pnpm kept BOTH copies, and every type that crosses a package boundary (ReadContract, WidthedConfidence, PrivateRestrictionBriefingItem) became TS2322 'not assignable to .../dist/read-contract/read-contract' between the two paths. The fix is to raise every manifest that declares the dependency at once (the engine's wave-6 commit did exactly that, 9 manifests), then re-resolve. Symptom to recognise: an error naming two node_modules/.pnpm/<pkg>@<v1>_... and <pkg>@<v2>_... paths for the same nominal type.

In LDT, `pnpm install` ends with `preinstall` calling `sh -c ...`; on this Windows seat `sh` is missing, so the very last step errors 'Failed' AFTER linking completes. Do not read that as a broken install. Complete it with `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` and confirm with the actual question: every workspace package's `node_modules/@empressaio/atom-contract/package.json` must report the SAME version (a stale `.pnpm/<pkg>@<old>` directory may linger harmlessly).

A local api-server typecheck cannot be trusted in LDT until the libs are built: without them it fails with TS6305 'Output file ... has not been built from source file'. `pnpm run typecheck:libs` (tsc --build) first, then `npx tsc -p artifacts/api-server/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, gives a CI-equivalent check in under a minute and caught this class of failure without waiting on CI.
